messages:
maya: quick idea — want feedback on a small RFC: add a Transport Adapter layer between the weight source and loader. goal: unify signed-URL S3 pulls, internal blobstore, on-prem NFS, and a future p2p cache under one async streaming contract.

zach: sounds promising. main win is plug-and-play for new stores w/o touching loader logic, right?

maya: exactly. plus standardize resumable streaming, per-chunk integrity, and a small metadata handshake so loader can choose zero-copy vs buffered. avoids ad-hoc range hacks.

li: can you sketch the interface? i worry about backpressure and memory spikes if we stream badly.

maya: sketch below (very rough):
```python
class TransportAdapter:
    # stat returns size, etag/mtime, support flags
    def stat(path) -> {"size": int, "etag": str, "supports_range": bool}

    # async iterator yields (offset, bytes, checksum) until done
    async def stream(path, start_offset=0):
        yield (offset, chunk_bytes, crc32_hex)

    # optional: return a signed url or local path for mmap fast-path
    def presign(path, ttl_secs=60) -> str|None
```

sasha: neat. two immediate questions: 1) how do we verify partial chunks? 2) when do we prefer mmap vs streaming?

maya: answers: 1) each chunk carries a CRC32/sha1 and we have a per-shard manifest with chunk-checksums (manifest can be produced at checkpoint time). loader verifies as it writes to the shard buffer; mismatch -> retry with backoff and maybe switch adapter. 2) prefer mmap when presign returns a local file scheme (file://) or when adapter exposes an fd/handle. streaming used for remote blobs and for decompress-on-the-fly.

li: what about atomicity and partial writes during warmup? we need the ability to mark a shard as "hydrating" and avoid serving partially written weights to the runtime.

maya: agreed. plan: loader writes to a temp path/buffer and only swaps in after full shard verify. for KV cache prefix warmup we can let partial prefixes be consumable if the runtime supports fallback, but that's a separate API flag.

zach: how do we handle range support differences? S3 signed urls have ranges, GCS too, but some internal stores don't.

maya: adapter exposes supports_range and a recommended chunk_size. If range isn't supported adapter must stream from zero and we use a buffered cache. we also add a lightweight manifest for chunk offsets to enable parallel fetch across adapters that support ranges.

sasha: latency question — streaming small chunks adds RTTs. do we prefer larger multi-MB chunks?

maya: yes: default chunk size is 4MB but adapters can recommend based on observed RTT and throughput. we should also support a small head-fetch (first N bytes) to read shard header and plan hot segments.

li: what about integrity across compressed transports (gz, zstd)? checksums should be on the post-decompress data, right?

maya: yes. manifest checksums are on the logical shard bytes (post-decompress, post-transforms). adapters that compress on the wire must supply checksums for the decompressed payload. we also include an adapter-level transform hook: decompress(data) -> bytes so loader doesn't duplicate codec logic.

zach: edge case: on-prem NFS can be flakey and hung mounts cause timeouts. adapters should implement timeouts, exponential backoff, and a health probe so the orchestration layer can evict bad adapters.

maya: noted. plan to standardize errors: RetriesTransient, RetriesExhausted, Fatal, NotFound. orchestration interprets those and can failover to a different adapter or to a degraded model variant.

sasha: how to surface metrics? per-chunk latency, retry counts, bytes/read, adapter id — useful for Optimize and Console.

maya: transport adapters emit structured events to the trace pipeline: adapter_name, shard_id, chunk_offset, duration_ms, bytes, result_code. we can then show hot paths and recommend batching/quantization changes.

li: any security concerns? signed urls leak risks, presigns TTL etc.

maya: adapter must support s3/v4 creds rotation, short-lived presigns, and an optional audit header that's stored with manifests. also, for private deployments we provide an HSM-backed signing adapter.

zach: fallback story? if streaming fails mid-shard do we retry from last good offset?

maya: yes — resumable tokens. adapter.stream can accept resume_token (opaque string) produced by previous session. token encodes last verified offset and adapter-specific state. if resume not possible, loader falls back to restart from zero or try another adapter.

sasha: can we avoid copy when adapter is local and the kernel supports splice/mremap?

maya: adapter can expose a fast-path: presign->file:// or an fd handle. loader will mmap or splice directly into device memory. we document kernel requirements and fall back to buffered write if unavailable.

deploy-bot: deploy:ci triggered transport-adapter-integration-tests job #421 (queued) :gear:

li: next steps? I'd like a quick RFC doc with the interface + error model + metrics + example adapters (s3/gcs/http/file/p2p). also include a tiny compatibility shim for existing loaders.

maya: thanks — i'll draft the short RFC today. plan: prototype S3 adapter + local-file adapter, wire the manifest checksums, and run warmup perf tests. will ping when PR is up. :thumbsup:

sasha: :+1: keep it minimal at first, we can iterate on the transform hook separately.

eng-bot: reminder: please add the RFC link to the eng-ml RFC board and tag arch-reviewers when ready.
